newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on Dalian.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on Dalian.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Wednesday on speculative buying boosted by a strong performance of Dalian soybeans, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 3,403 yuan ($410) per tonne, rising 13 yuan. It opened at 3,396 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 3,380 and a high of 3,407 yuan.
May fell 25 to 3,345, September rose 22 to 3,407, November was up 30 to 3,430 and January 1998 contract fell 10 to 3,430.
Combined volume rose to 23,000 tonnes from 15,800 yuan.
Traders said the recent strong performance of soybeans on the Dalian Commodities Exchange boosted the confidence of long position holders in Shanghai.
"Market sentiment has improved gradually on speculative buying," one trader said.
"But institutional investors are still on the sidelines because there is no market-moving news," he added.
Traders expected soybeans to rise slowly in the next few days.
